name: Static quads
equipment: a rolled towel or a foam roller
movement: the knee bent over a roll, straightened until the leg is in a line with the heel off the floor and the toes pulled up, held, lowered

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to where you will be.

words.hint: Lying with a roll under the knee: straighten the leg, toes up, hold five seconds.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Lie on your back side on to it, a rolled towel or foam roller under one knee.
words.position: Lie on your back, side on to the phone. A rolled towel or a foam roller under the working knee, so the knee is bent over it and the heel rests on the floor. The other leg straight along the floor.
words.top: The leg straight in one line, the heel lifted off the floor, the toes pulled up toward you, for the count.
howto: Lie on your back with a rolled towel or a foam roller under one knee. The knee should be bent over it: if the leg is still nearly straight, prop the knee higher.
Pull the toes of that foot back toward you and straighten the knee, lifting the heel off the floor until the leg is in one line.
Hold for the count — five seconds — breathing.
Lower the heel back to the floor and let the thigh go before the next one.
words.cannot: How hard the thigh is working: it sees the knee straighten and the toes come up, which go with the contraction. Press as hard as is comfortable.
words.about: Static quads over a roll — lying on your back side on: the knee angle between hip and ankle, 150 or so at rest over the roll and 180 straight; a rep is under way past 165 and counts when the knee is back under 160; at the top the knee at least 170 and the foot's angle at the heel, between toe and knee, 100 or less with the toes pulled up. Between reps the knee must rest under 160, or the roll is too low. Hold five seconds at the top.
words.lost: Lie down side on to the camera, whole body in
words.early: Hold it straight for the full count next time
words.safety: Nothing should hurt. The roll takes the knee out of full extension, which is what makes this gentle: keep it under the knee, not the thigh or the calf.
words.easier: A shorter hold; a lower roll.
words.harder: A longer hold; a bigger roll; an ankle weight.
words.mistakes: Lifting the whole leg from the hip instead of straightening the knee; forgetting to pull the toes up; letting the roll slip down the calf.

measurements.label: knee angle

settings.label: Knee angle at the top, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.why: The knee between hip and ankle: bent over the roll at rest, 150 or so; 180 straight. The progress measurement, rising through the rep. At the top at least 170.

measurements.label: knee at rest

settings.label: Knee at rest, at most (the roll is too low past this)

measurements.why: The same angle, judged only between reps: the knee must rest bent over the roll, under 160. Past that the roll is too low or has slipped, and the exercise is a leg raise, not a quad set.

measurements.label: toe, heel, knee

settings.label: Foot angle at the top, at most (toes pulled up)

measurements.why: The foot against the shin, at the heel: relaxed it reads 110–125, toes pulled up 100 or less. Judged at the top.

ready.nudge: Bend the knee over a rolled towel or a foam roller — if the leg is still nearly straight, prop the knee higher

prompt.text: Straighten the knee — heel up, toes pulled toward you

faults.label: Prop the knee higher
faults.text: Prop the knee higher — a rolled towel or a foam roller under it
faults.deep: The leg is nearly straight at rest — put more under the knee

faults.label: Knee not straight
faults.text: Straighten the knee fully — the leg in one line
faults.deep: Tighten the thigh and lock the knee out

settings.label: Knee angle that counts as under way
